::: {.lead}
In Lecture 1 you learned the types of digital media, the tetrad, the jobs
of game media and the production pipeline. Today you use all four on a
game that you play. There are no new ideas: two short problems. Do each one
alone. The results of the activities are at the end of this worksheet.
:::

## Recall

- **Digital media:** text, images, audio, video, animation and interactive
  content.
- The **tetrad**: mechanics, story, aesthetics and technology make the
  player experience together.
- Media do five jobs: **feedback**, **guidance**, **mood**, **story**,
  **identity**. The team makes them in a **pipeline**: pre-production,
  production, post-production.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="story|pre-production"}
A chime and a flash when the player collects a coin. Which job?
:   feedback

The phone, the engine and the screen. Which element of the tetrad?
:   technology

Recording the voice of the hero. Which stage of the pipeline?
:   production
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Take your game apart

A studio wants to know why your favourite game works. The first step of an
analysis is a list: which media are there, and what does each element of
the tetrad look like in this game? @fig-screen shows the media of one
screen of *Ember Trail*.

![The media of one game screen.](images/annotated-screen.png){#fig-screen width=90%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Media and tetrad · 15 min"}
Choose a game on your phone. Take a screenshot of one busy moment.

1. Write five media elements of the game, and the type of each one.
2. Write one line for each element of the tetrad: mechanics, story,
   aesthetics, technology.

*Your product:* a table of five elements and four short lines.

::: {.check}
A good answer: "The hero (image), the battle music (audio), the coin
counter (text), the intro film (video), the hero running (animation).
Mechanics: tap to jump. Story: the hero looks for his sister. Aesthetics:
bright cartoon colours and drums. Technology: a phone, held upright."
Check: five elements of different types, and one line for each element of
the tetrad.
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · What each element does, and how it was made

An analysis says what an element does for the player. "There is music in
the menu" only describes. "The slow flute music in the menu makes the
player calm before play begins" names the element, its job and its effect.
One element can have several jobs (@fig-jobs).

![One coin, three jobs.](images/media-functions.png){#fig-jobs width=90%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Jobs and pipeline · 15 min"}
Use your table from Activity 1.

1. Choose three elements. For each one, write its job and its effect on
   the player in one sentence.
2. Choose one of the three. Write what the team did for it in
   pre-production, production and post-production.

*Your product:* three sentences and three short pipeline lines.

::: {.check}
A good sentence: "The red flash when the hero is hit is feedback: it tells
me at once that I lost health, so I play more carefully." Good pipeline
lines for the battle music: "Pre-production: the team plans a fast tune.
Production: a composer records it. Post-production: the team mixes it so
that the sound effects stay clear, and exports it." Check: the element, its
job and its effect in each sentence; the three stages in order.
:::
:::

## Exercises

1. Name the six types of digital media.
2. Turn this description into an analysis: "There is rain in level 3."
3. Can one element have several jobs? Give an example.
4. In which stage of the pipeline does the team write the script?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. Text, images, audio, video, animation, interactive content.
2. For example: "The sound of rain in level 3 sets a sad mood, so the
   player feels alone."
3. Yes. For example, the splash of a jump is feedback, mood and identity.
4. In pre-production.
:::
